transcript: Every PowerPoint to video converter makes different trade-offs. Before you pick one, ask the right questions, so the tool fits your work.
Start with the job the video must do. Who's watching, where it will live, how often it changes, and how sensitive the content is will decide most things.
Next, narration: record it or write it. If your deck changes often, narration from your speaker notes is easier, because fixing a sentence means editing text, not re-recording.
For sensitive material, check your organisation's policy before uploading. Then preview a real deck, not a demo, and ask: does it improve your story, or just play it back?
Look for timing that follows the speech, captions for viewers with the sound off, an MP4 your platform accepts, and clear limits on price and watermarks.
Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out. Try it first on Basic, no subscription needed, or go Pro and let a.i. direct it. Visit powerpoint2vid.com.
